fr.elements: Main Building; Detached Structure; Front Driveway; Access Road; Open Green Space; Landscaped Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Scattered Vegetation; Open Terrain; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Long Driveway; Single Access Point; Limited Rear Access; Open Terrain; Dense Vegetation
fr.recommendations: Confirming clear and unobstructed travel along the driveway and access road could improve response times and apparatus movement, particularly given the extended travel distance from the street to the main building. Because the property has a single access point, ensuring that the driveway remains wide enough to support simultaneous ingress and egress of emergency vehicles would support more effective operations. Providing visible address marking at the street frontage may assist responders in locating the property quickly. Coordinating with local fire or emergency services to familiarize responding units with the layout, including the detached structure and limited rear access, could further enhance operational readiness during an incident.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Shrubs; Heavy Brush; Fuel Continuity; Mixed Vegetation Cover; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Brushland Interface; Open Terrain; Long Driveway; Vegetation Adjacent to Structure; Defensible Space; Wildland Interface
wildfire.recommendations: Reducing the density of heavy brush and managing scattered shrubs within the immediate structure perimeter could improve defensible space and reduce fuel continuity between the surrounding brushland and the residence. Where vegetation grows in close proximity to the structure, increasing separation between plant material and exterior surfaces may reduce structure exposure and support suppression operations. Managing vegetation within the tree cluster areas to reduce ladder fuel opportunities, and thinning connections between scattered trees and adjacent brush, could further reduce fuel continuity across the property. The long driveway should be maintained to support firefighter access and evacuation, with vegetation along its edges kept trimmed to preserve clearance and visibility. Existing open terrain areas represent a natural fuel break that should be preserved and maintained. Ongoing vegetation management within the mixed cover zones near improvements would support long-term wildfire resilience and property preparedness at this wildland interface location.
